items.followUp: State two functions of vitamin A.

rubric.why: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus.
rubric.description: States that vitamin D promotes calcium and phosphorus absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its role in absorption of both minerals from the intestine.

rubric.why: Vitamin D is needed for healthy bones and teeth and helps prevent rickets.
rubric.description: States a bone- or teeth-related function of vitamin D.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning bone or teeth development/strength, or prevention of rickets.

modelAnswer: Vitamin D helps the intestine absorb calcium and phosphorus.
It is essential for healthy bones and teeth and helps prevent rickets.

items.followUp: State the approximate weight and length of an adult human heart.

rubric.why: An adult human liver weighs approximately 1.5 kg.
rubric.description: Gives the approximate weight of the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 1.5 kg.

rubric.why: The liver is approximately 20 cm in size.
rubric.description: Gives the approximate size of the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 20 cm.

modelAnswer: The adult human liver weighs about 1.5 kg.
It is about 20 cm in size.

items.followUp: State one function each of eosinophils and lymphocytes.

rubric.why: Neutrophils defend the body by engulfing and digesting invading microbes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for phagocytosis or engulfing and destroying bacteria/pathogens.

rubric.why: Basophils release histamine and heparin, which are involved in inflammation and blood clotting control.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that basophils release histamine or heparin.

modelAnswer: Neutrophils engulf and destroy bacteria and other pathogens by phagocytosis.
Basophils release histamine and heparin; these substances are involved in inflammation and help prevent blood clotting.

items.followUp: What are root hairs, and how do they help a plant absorb water?

rubric.why: Root hairs are extensions of cells in the root epidermis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as extensions of root epidermal cells.

rubric.why: Root hairs absorb water and mineral salts and increase the root's absorbing surface area.
rubric.description: States the function of root hairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for water and mineral absorption, or for explaining their increased absorbing surface area.

modelAnswer: Root hairs are thin extensions of the epidermal cells of a root.
They absorb water and mineral salts from the soil and increase the root's surface area for absorption.

items.followUp: Write any two measures that help prevent malaria.

rubric.why: Removing stagnant water prevents mosquitoes from breeding.
rubric.description: Gives a measure that prevents mosquito breeding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for removing or draining stagnant water.

rubric.why: Avoiding mosquito bites or preventing mosquitoes from entering homes reduces dengue transmission.
rubric.description: Gives a measure that reduces contact with mosquitoes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable measure, such as nets, repellents, insecticides, or covering water containers.

modelAnswer: Remove stagnant water from around homes so mosquitoes cannot breed.
Use mosquito nets or repellents, or cover water containers to reduce mosquito contact and breeding.

items.followUp: Explain the ecosystem level and biosphere level of biological organization, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A population consists of members of the same species living in a particular area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a population as individuals of one species in the same area.

rubric.why: A named group of one species in an area is an example of a population.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as deer in a forest or fish of one species in a pond.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living together in an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a community as populations of different species in the same area.

rubric.why: A community example includes different species living together in one place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as plants and animals in a pond or forest.

modelAnswer: Population level: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
Example: Deer of the same species living in a forest form a population.
Community level: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.
Example: The populations of plants, animals and microorganisms living in a pond form a community.

items.followUp: What are simple tissues? Describe the structure and function of parenchyma and collenchyma.

rubric.why: A compound tissue is made of more than one type of cell working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that compound tissues contain different cell types working together.

rubric.why: Xylem conducts water and mineral salts from roots to the rest of the plant, especially the leaves.
rubric.description: States the transport function of xylem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the upward transport of water and mineral salts from roots.

rubric.why: Xylem includes vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and fibres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two xylem cell types or components.

rubric.why: Phloem transports prepared food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
rubric.description: States the transport function of phloem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the transport of food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

rubric.why: Phloem includes sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and fibres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two phloem cell types or components.

modelAnswer: Compound tissues are made of more than one type of cell working together to perform a function.
Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves and other parts of the plant.
Xylem consists of vessels, tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres; most xylem elements are dead at maturity, except the parenchyma.
Phloem transports prepared food from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

items.followUp: Write a note on two causes and two effects of air pollution.

rubric.why: Trees are cut to obtain timber or fuel, contributing to deforestation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for tree cutting, logging, or clearing forests for timber or fuel.

rubric.why: Forests are cleared to make farmland, roads and settlements or to expand cities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid cause such as agricultural expansion, urbanization or construction.

rubric.why: Without trees, soil is less protected and erosion and flooding can increase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for soil erosion, loss of fertile soil or increased flooding.

rubric.why: Deforestation destroys habitats and can reduce biodiversity; it can also contribute to climate change and disrupt the water cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid effect such as habitat or biodiversity loss, climate change, or disruption of the water cycle.

modelAnswer: Causes: Forests are cut down for timber and fuel.
Forests are also cleared for agriculture, roads, settlements and urban expansion.
Effects: Removal of trees exposes the soil, causing soil erosion and increasing the risk of floods.
Deforestation destroys habitats and reduces biodiversity; it also contributes to climate change and disrupts the water cycle.
